case_name: Asharam And Another v State Of Madhya Pradesh

State Of Madhya Pradesh

facts: The appellants stand convicted under Section 307/149 IPC and sentenced to undergo 5 years R.I. and a fine of Rs. 5000/- to each accused.
On 31.10.1988 Nandan (PW-1), Tikaram (PW-2), and Koshabai (PW-3) had gone to sow the seeds in their field.
After sowing the seeds, when they were returning to their village, they saw the appellants along with three others hiding in the field of Chunni come out of the hiding and assaulted Nandan (PW-1).
When Tikaram (PW-2) and Koshabai (PW-3) came to the rescue of Nandan, they were also beaten up.

All the three were taken to the village Bijadehi and the FIR was lodged by PW-1 at Police Station, Bijadehi at 4:00 p.m. where the offence was registered under Sections 147, 148, 149, 324 and 307 IPC.
issues: Whether an accused committed an offence under Section 307/149 as a member of unlawful assembly and in furtherance of their intention, attempted to murder Nandan, Tikaram and Kaushabai by causing deadly injuries.
petitioner_arguments: The FIR was ante- timing and unreliable.

PW-1 had totally denied of having gone to Police Station, Bijadehi to lodge the report and, on the contrary, PW-1 had deposed in his evidence before the court that he had become unconscious and had regained consciousness on 31.10.1988 only in the night.
When PW-1 was the star witness who stated that he did not lodge the FIR as he was unconscious throughout the day, it was clear that the said FIR was fabricated.
There were serious contradictions in the evidence inter se all these witnesses, the FIR was not reliable.
respondent_arguments: The complainant party was badly beaten, they were left unconscious on the spot, the accused thought that the complainant party was dead upon which they fled and, therefore, intention of the accused party stood duly established.
The appellants along with three others were hiding in the field of Chunni where the incident is alleged to have taken place.
court_reasoning: There were serious contradictions in the evidence inter se all these witnesses, the FIR was not reliable.

PW-1 had totally denied of having gone to Police Station, Bijadehi to lodge the report and, on the contrary, PW-1 had deposed in his evidence before the court that he had become unconscious and had regained consciousness on 31.10.1988 only in the night.
The story given in the FIR did not tally with what was stated before the court by PW-1.
holding: The accused were given the benefit of doubt and acquitted the accused of the charges under Section 307/149 IPC.
